blocks.text: SFT and RLHF, both covered in depth in earlier modules of this course, get compared constantly because they represent two different stages in a typical fine-tuning pipeline, this topic pulls that comparison into one place, covering what each stage actually optimizes for and why most production pipelines use both rather than choosing one over the other.

The short version is that SFT teaches a model to imitate labeled examples, while RLHF further refines that model toward outputs humans actually prefer, two different training signals that are usually complementary rather than substitutes.
1. What Each One Optimizes For
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913814-413670404.png

SFT, covered in an earlier module, trains a model to imitate specific labeled instruction and response examples directly, RLHF, covered in the earlier Alignment Training module, instead optimizes a model toward whichever outputs a reward signal, ultimately derived from human preferences, ranks more highly, a genuinely different training objective.
2. SFT Training Data Shape
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913814-313484535.png

SFT needs direct instruction and response pairs, covered in the earlier Instruction Following topic, where each example shows exactly what a good response looks like for a given input, the model learns by directly imitating these labeled examples.

code.content: {"instruction": "Summarize this article in two sentences", "response": "The article discusses..."}

blocks.text: 3. RLHF Training Data Shape and Process

blocks.alt: RLHF Training Data Shape and Process
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913815-141852750.png

RLHF, covered in earlier topics, needs preference comparisons rather than single correct examples, a reward model first learns to predict which of two responses humans would prefer, then PPO, also covered in an earlier topic, uses that reward model to actually update the policy model toward higher-reward outputs, a meaningfully more involved multi-stage process than SFT single training pass.
4. Why Pipelines Typically Use Both
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913815-439805510.png

SFT establishes basic instruction-following competence, teaching a model the expected format and general task behavior, RLHF then refines that already-competent model further, polishing response quality and aligning it with more nuanced human preferences that are hard to fully capture in a fixed set of labeled examples.
5. What Skipping RLHF Looks Like
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472913816-885605301.png

A model trained with SFT alone generally follows the expected format and completes tasks reasonably, but often lacks the more refined judgment, tone, and preference alignment that RLHF specifically targets, many capable models ship with SFT only when the added complexity of RLHF is not justified for the use case, this is a legitimate choice, not automatically a mistake.

blocks.text: 6. Complexity and Stability Tradeoff
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914121-30856560.png

SFT is comparatively simple to run, a single supervised training pass with well understood stability properties, RLHF full pipeline, reward model training followed by PPO, has more hyperparameters, more moving parts, and a real risk of training instability if not carefully tuned, covered in the earlier RLHF and PPO topics.

blocks.title: This complexity difference is why DPO and similar methods gained popularity
blocks.content: Methods like DPO and ORPO, both covered in the Alignment Training module, emerged specifically to capture much of RLHF preference alignment benefit while avoiding the added complexity and instability risk of the full reward-model-plus-PPO pipeline.

blocks.text: 7. Data Collection Cost Differences
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914122-22771701.png

SFT data collection means writing or curating correct example responses, RLHF data collection means having humans compare pairs of responses and indicate which is preferred, a different kind of labeling effort that is sometimes faster per judgment, since comparing is often easier than writing a perfect response from scratch, but still adds a distinct collection process on top of SFT.
8. Choosing Where to Invest Given Limited Resources

For a team with limited data collection and training budget, a well executed SFT stage on carefully curated examples often provides the largest single quality improvement, RLHF or a lighter alternative like DPO tends to provide meaningful additional polish once the SFT foundation is already solid.
9. This Comparison in an Interview Context

When this comparison comes up in a system design or interview setting, the strongest answer usually explains both what each stage optimizes for and why they are typically sequential and complementary rather than picking one as universally better, exactly the framing covered throughout this topic.
Worked Example

A team fine-tuning an internal coding assistant starts with an SFT stage on curated coding instruction and response pairs, producing a model that reliably follows the expected format and solves straightforward requests.

Noticing the model sometimes produces technically correct but stylistically inconsistent code, they add an RLHF stage using preference comparisons between different code style choices, refining the model toward the team preferred conventions in a way the original SFT examples alone did not fully capture.
Common Mistakes

items: Treating SFT and RLHF as competing alternatives rather than typically sequential, complementary stages
Jumping straight to RLHF without a solid SFT foundation, skipping the basic instruction-following competence it establishes
Underestimating the added complexity and instability risk of a full RLHF pipeline compared to SFT
Assuming RLHF is always necessary, when a well executed SFT stage alone is sufficient for many use cases

blocks.text: Practice

For a fine-tuning project you are familiar with or could imagine, explain in your own words what specific quality gap RLHF would address that SFT alone would leave unaddressed, using the imitation-versus-preference-optimization framing covered in this topic.
Key Takeaway

SFT trains a model to imitate labeled instruction and response examples while RLHF further optimizes it toward human preference judgments through a reward model and PPO, and the two are typically sequential and complementary, SFT establishing base competence and RLHF refining alignment further, rather than being alternative choices for the same training goal.
